lesson.title: Greet someone
lesson.scenario: Your partner introduces you to a friend of a similar age at their home. Greet each other, introduce yourselves, then thank the host for welcoming you.
lesson.unitTitle: Meet someone and keep the exchange going

introduction.goal: Greet a peer and thank them for their welcome.

line.targetText: ខ្ញុំឈ្មោះ Sam។
ខ្ញុំឈ្មោះ Alex។

introduction.usageNote: Keep the greeting, thank-you and attention-getter attached to their situations. The formal greeting is a recognition contrast; this casual scene does not require it.
introduction.dialectNote: Target model: contemporary Cambodian Khmer with a Phnom Penh reference. This candidate has no verified model speaker. Same-age peer address is provisional; do not generalize it to older relatives or formal settings.

teachingCards.title: Greet a peer
teachingCards.note: Use this candidate for a casual meeting between adults of similar age. Review the greeting and setting together; this is not a universal address rule.
teachingCards.recallCue: You meet a friend of your partner. Offer a casual hello.

teachingCards.title: Thank someone
teachingCards.note: Use this after someone helps you. It acknowledges help rather than asking for new information.
teachingCards.recallCue: Someone repeats their name for you. Thank them.

teachingCards.title: Get someone’s attention
teachingCards.note: This candidate marks an apology or excuse me. Review the situation and intonation before recording it; it does not itself ask for repetition.
teachingCards.recallCue: Politely get someone’s attention before asking for help.

teachingCards.title: Recognize a formal greeting
teachingCards.note: Keep the formal greeting distinct from the casual scene. A fluent reviewer must confirm when it fits; recognition here is not a cultural etiquette assessment.
teachingCards.recallCue: You need to recognize the formal greeting from this lesson.
